James decides to run 3 sprints 3 times a week.  He runs 60 meters each sprint.  How many total meters does he run a week?

To determine the total distance James runs in a week, we need to calculate the distance he runs each time he runs 3 sprints and then multiply that by the number of sprints he performs each week.

1. Calculate the distance James runs each time he runs 3 sprints:
   \[
   \text{Distance per sprint} = 60 \text{ meters}
   \]
   \[
   \text{Distance per session} = 3 \text{ sprints} \times 60 \text{ meters/sprint} = 180 \text{ meters}
   \]

2. Calculate the total distance for one week:
   \[
   \text{Distance per week} = \text{Distance per session} \times \text{Number of sessions per week}
   \]
   \[
   \text{Distance per week} = 180 \text{ meters/session} \times 3 \text{ sessions/week} = 540 \text{ meters/week}
   \]

Therefore, the total distance James runs in a week is \(\boxed{540}\) meters.
